blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence: `src/main.rs` accepts `--quiet` before the file and passes it to
findings.location: design.md#Decision: The progress reporter takes a `quiet` switch
findings.recommendation: The requirement and its scenarios only cover `ledger import --quiet <file>`. `src/main.rs` matches the arguments by exact shape (`[command, path] if command == "import"`), so a script that writes `ledger import data.csv --quiet` would, as designed, fall into the usage branch and exit 2 without importing anything. Either state in the requirement where the flag is accepted and add a scenario for the other placement (accepted, or rejected with the usage error and exit code 2), or accept it in both positions and say so.
findings.title: The position of `--quiet` on the command line is left unspecified

findings.recommendation: The change adds a user-visible option to the `ledger import` command line and targets nightly scripts' mail reports, yet every domain is left unticked with no reason on its line. Whether a CLI flag falls under `user-interface` and a scheduled job's output under `operations` depends on how the project defines those domains; tick them so their experts review the plan, or keep them unticked with a reason (`- [ ] operations — <why>`).
findings.title: No domain is ticked or justified in the proposal
